gloss: be many, be great; many, much, great; chief; multitude; ten thousand
summary: The root is number and size: to be many or great (Psa 3:2; 104:24). רַב is many as against מְעַט few (Num 26:54; 1Sa 14:6), great or abounding, as Yahweh is רַב־חֶסֶד, “abounding in steadfast love” (Exo 34:6), the elder of two (Gen 25:23), and, said alone, “enough!” (Deu 1:6; 1Ki 19:4); as a noun it is the chief of a body of men (2Ki 25:8), the word behind the New Testament’s Rabbi. רֹב is multitude or abundance, and רְבָבָה and רִבּוֹ the greatest number counted, ten thousand, set beside אֶלֶף “thousand” (Lev 26:8; Num 10:36). Arabic rabb “lord” and rubba “myriad”, Ugaritic rb “great, chief” and rbt “ten thousand”, Phoenician rb “many; chief” and Akkadian rabû “great; chief” have the same senses; a verb “shoot” and its noun “archer” share the spelling, but their tie to the root is not clear.

words.gloss: many, much; great, abounding; elder; enough
words.summary: Many in number, much or great in amount, size or degree; of two, the elder. Said alone or with לְ, רַב is “enough”, a thing gone on long enough.

senses.definition: More in number: many days, peoples, waters or persons; set against מְעַט, few.

evidence.note: “To the רַב you shall increase his inheritance, and to the מְעַט you shall diminish his inheritance”: many against few.
“There is no restraint to Yahweh to save בְּרַב אוֹ בִמְעָט, by many or by few.”
The spies are to see whether the people is “few or רָב”.
Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines יָמִים רַבִּים, many days.
“You shall not follow רַבִּים to do evil”: the many, the majority.
Wealth adds רֵעִים רַבִּים, many friends.
He shall judge between עַמִּים רַבִּים, many peoples, beside “strong nations”.
“By his knowledge my righteous servant shall make לָרַבִּים righteous, and he shall bear their iniquities.”
“He bore the sin of רַבִּים.” Quoted at Heb 9:28 (πολλῶν).
“Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many”, the words of Isa 53:12.
“To give his life a ransom for many”, after Isa 53:11–12.
“And רַבִּים of those sleeping in the dust of the ground shall awake.”
Those who turn הָרַבִּים, the many, to righteousness shall shine as the stars.

senses.definition: Great in amount, size or degree: a great deep, much water, great wickedness; in the construct, abounding in a thing.

evidence.note: Yahweh saw that the wickedness of man was רַבָּה in the earth.
All the fountains of תְּהוֹם רַבָּה, the great deep, were broken up.
Yahweh proclaims himself “slow to anger and רַב־חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת, abounding in steadfast love and truth”.
“How רַב is your goodness, which you have stored up for those who fear you!”
His compassions are new every morning: “רַבָּה is your faithfulness”.
Mount Zion, “the city of מֶלֶךְ רָב, the great king”, which Jesus names at Mat 5:35.
“Nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King”: Psa 48:3.
“Yahweh is over מַיִם רַבִּים, many waters.”
The voice of the glory of the God of Israel “like the voice of מַיִם רַבִּים”, as Rev 1:15 and 14:2.
No king is saved by רָב־חָיִל, a great army.

senses.definition: Of two brothers or peoples, the elder, set against צָעִיר, the younger.

evidence.note: “And רַב shall serve צָעִיר”: the elder the younger.
Paul quotes it: “The elder (ὁ μείζων) shall serve the younger.”

senses.definition: Alone, or with לְ and a person (רַב לָכֶם), “much”, and so “enough”: a thing has gone on long enough, or a person has gone far enough.

evidence.note: “רַב לָכֶם, you have dwelt long enough at this mountain.” Also Deu 2:3.
Yahweh to Moses: “רַב לָךְ; speak no more to me of this matter.”
Elijah under the broom tree: “רַב! Now, Yahweh, take my life.”
Yahweh to the destroying angel: “רַב; now stay your hand.”
Israel: “רַב! Joseph my son is still alive.”
Korah’s company to Moses and Aaron: “רַב לָכֶם, you take too much upon you”; Moses answers them with the same words (Num 16:7).
“רַב לָכֶם, princes of Israel! Remove violence and spoil.”

evidence.locator: Isa.53.11, לָֽרַבִּים → πολλοῖς; Isa.53.12, רַבִּים → πολλῶν; Ezk.43.2 and Psa.29.3, מַיִם רַבִּים → ὑδάτων πολλῶν; πολύς renders רַב ×286

evidence.note: “To bear the sins of πολλῶν”, Isa 53:12.
A ransom ἀντὶ πολλῶν.
“By the obedience of one shall οἱ πολλοί be made righteous”, after Isa 53:11.
His voice “as the sound of ὑδάτων πολλῶν”, Ezk 43:2.

evidence.locator: Psa.48.3 (LXX 47:3), מֶלֶךְ רָב → βασιλέως τοῦ μεγάλου; μέγας renders רַב ×28

evidence.note: “The city τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως”, Psa 48:3.
“ὁ μείζων shall serve the lesser”: Gen 25:23’s רַב.

parallels.note: “Mighty”, beside it of a people or nations.

evidence.note: “The people of the sons of Israel is רַב וְעָצוּם, more and mightier than we.”
“I will divide him a portion with the many, and he shall divide the spoil with the mighty.”

phrases.gloss: enough for you; you have gone far enough

words.summary: The great one of a body of men, and so its chief: a title in construct with the men he is over, most of all at the courts of Assyria and Babylon, whose own titles (Akkadian rab šāqê, rab ša-rēši) Hebrew takes over. The New Testament’s Rabbi and Rabboni, “my master”, are this word.

senses.gloss: chief, captain (of a body of men)
senses.definition: The head of a group, named in construct with those he is over: the chief of the guard, of the eunuchs, of the sailors; in the plural, a king’s chief officers.

evidence.note: Nebuzaradan, רַב־טַבָּחִים, chief of the guard, servant of the king of Babylon.
Nebuzaradan רַב־טַבָּחִים, Nebushazban רַב־סָרִיס, Nergal-sharezer רַב־מָג, “and all רַבֵּי the king of Babylon”, his chief officers.
רַב הַחֹבֵל, the chief of the sailors, the shipmaster, wakes Jonah.
Ashpenaz, רַב סָרִיסָיו, the chief of Nebuchadnezzar’s eunuchs.
The king commanded “every רַב of his house”, his officers, to do as each guest pleased.
Ishmael, of the royal seed, “and רַבֵּי הַמֶּלֶךְ”, the king’s chief men.

senses.gloss: Rabshakeh, Rab-saris, Rab-mag (Assyrian and Babylonian titles)
senses.definition: Court titles of Assyria and Babylon taken over whole: רַב־שָׁקֵה, Akkadian rab šāqê, “chief cupbearer”; רַב־סָרִיס, rab ša-rēši, “chief eunuch”; and רַב־מָג, an office of Babylon whose second part is not clear.

evidence.note: The king of Assyria sends the Tartan, רַב־סָרִיס and רַב־שָׁקֵה from Lachish to Hezekiah.
The king of Assyria sent רַב־שָׁקֵה with a great army.
רַב־שָׁקֵה cries in Judean to the men on the wall.
Among Babylon’s princes at the middle gate: Sarsechim רַב־סָרִיס, Nergal-sharezer רַב־מָג.

senses.definition: In the New Testament’s Aramaic, רַבִּי, “my master”, a title of address to a teacher, which John explains as “Teacher”.

evidence.note: “Rabbi (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), where are you staying?”
Mary: “Rabboni, which is to say, Teacher.”
The scribes love to be called “Rabbi, Rabbi”; “but be not you called Rabbi, for one is your teacher, the Christ, and all you are brothers”.
Nicodemus: “Rabbi, we know you are a teacher come from God.”
John the Baptist’s disciples call him Rabbi.
“(Heb. and Aram. רַבִּי, my master)”; “a title of respectful address to Jewish teachers”: of John, Jo 3:26; of Christ, Mt 26:25, 49; Mk 9:5 and often in John.
“Ῥαββί, which is to say, being interpreted, Διδάσκαλε.”
Judas: “Hail, Rabbi”, and kissed him.
“(Aram. רַבּוֹנִי, later, רִבּוֹנִי, my master)”: Mk 10:51; Jo 20:16.
“Ῥαββουνί, which is to say, Διδάσκαλε.”
Bartimaeus: “Rabboni, that I may receive my sight.”

words.summary: The many-ness or greatness of a thing: a multitude of people or years, abundance of goods, the greatness of God’s steadfast love. לָרֹב is “in abundance”, more than can be counted.

senses.definition: A great number, of people, years, words or sacrifices; set against מְעֹט, fewness.

evidence.note: “According to רֹב the years you shall increase its price, and according to מְעֹט the years you shall diminish it.”
Hagar’s seed “shall not be counted מֵרֹב, for multitude”.
Seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered מֵרֹב.
A great people that cannot be numbered or counted מֵרֹב.
“Days should speak, and רֹב שָׁנִים should teach wisdom”: many years, parallel “days”.
Old men in Jerusalem’s streets, staff in hand מֵרֹב יָמִים, for great age.
“In רֹב דְּבָרִים, a multitude of words, transgression does not cease.” Also Ecc 5:2.
“In רֹב יוֹעֵץ, a multitude of counsellors, there is safety.”
“To what purpose is רֹב זִבְחֵיכֶם, the multitude of your sacrifices, to me?” says Yahweh.
No king is saved by בְּרָב־חָיִל, the multitude of an army.

senses.definition: Great amount or degree: abundance of goods or of peace; the greatness of God’s steadfast love, compassion, majesty.

evidence.note: “The meek shall inherit the land and delight themselves in רֹב שָׁלוֹם, abundance of peace”; Jesus takes up the first half at Mat 5:5.
“In רֹב חַסְדְּךָ, the abundance of your steadfast love, I will come into your house.”
“According to רֹב רַחֲמֶיךָ, the multitude of your compassions, blot out my transgressions.”
“According to רֹב חֲסָדָיו”, beside רַב־טוּב, great goodness, to the house of Israel.
“In רֹב גְּאוֹנְךָ, the greatness of your majesty, you overthrow those who rise against you.”
Praise him כְּרֹב גֻּדְלוֹ, according to the abundance of his greatness.
You did not serve Yahweh with joy “מֵרֹב כֹּל, for the abundance of everything”.

senses.gloss: לָרֹב: in abundance, in great number
senses.definition: With לְ, as an adverb: in abundance, beyond counting; often “as the stars” or “as the sand” לָרֹב.

evidence.note: “You are this day as the stars of heaven לָרֹב.”
Judah and Israel as the sand by the sea לָרֹב.
Solomon made cedars as the sycamores of the lowland לָרֹב.
Laban’s little had increased לָרֹב.
David prepared iron and bronze לָרֹב for the house.

evidence.locator: Psa.37.11 (LXX 36:11), רֹב שָׁלוֹם → πλήθει εἰρήνης; πλῆθος renders רֹב ×64

evidence.note: From one man “as the stars of the sky τῷ πλήθει”, Deu 1:10’s לָרֹב.

words.gloss: be many, become many; be great
words.summary: A rare verb beside the commoner רָבָה (entered under its own root): to be or become many, mostly of enemies, sins and works; in the pual, “made ten thousands”.

senses.definition: To be, or grow to be, many in number; often in exclamation, “how many are…!”

evidence.note: “Yahweh, how רַבּוּ my adversaries! Many (רַבִּים) rise up against me.”
“How רַבּוּ your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you have made them all.”
“They are more (רַבּוּ) than the locust, and there is no number to them.”
Those who hate me without cause are more than the hairs of my head.
“See my enemies, for they רַבּוּ.”
“Our backslidings רַבּוּ; we have sinned against you.”
The slain of Yahweh shall be many.
When man began לָרֹב, to multiply, on the face of the ground.
“Not מֵרֻבְּכֶם, because you were more than any people, did Yahweh set his love on you, for you were the fewest (הַמְעַט) of all peoples.”

senses.definition: To be great in degree.

evidence.note: “The outcry of Sodom and Gomorrah, for it רַבָּה, and their sin, for it is very heavy”: great, parallel כָּבְדָה.
“And the forsaking רַבָּה in the midst of the land.”
Lest the beasts of the field become many against you.

senses.definition: Of flocks, to be multiplied to ten thousands; a verb made from רְבָבָה, beside one made from אֶלֶף.

evidence.note: “Our sheep bringing forth thousands (מַאֲלִיפוֹת), מְרֻבָּבוֹת, ten thousands, in our fields.”

evidence.locator: Psa.3.2, רַבּוּ → ἐπληθύνθησαν; πληθύνω renders the verb ×8

evidence.note: The number of the disciples ἐπληθύνετο greatly in Jerusalem.

words.summary: Ten thousand, the next count above אֶלֶף, and so the largest round number: paired with “thousand” (Lev 26:8; Deu 32:30; 1Sa 18:7) and used for a host beyond counting. Moses’ word when the ark rested is “Return, Yahweh, to the רִבְבוֹת of the thousands of Israel” (Num 10:36).

senses.definition: The number ten thousand, ten times a thousand, counted next after אֶלֶף.

evidence.note: “Ten men of a hundred, a hundred of a thousand, and a thousand לָרְבָבָה, of ten thousand”: the scale counts on by tens.
“Five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall chase רְבָבָה”: five to a hundred, a hundred to ten thousand.
“How should one chase a thousand, and two put רְבָבָה to flight, unless their Rock had sold them?”
“Saul has struck his thousands, and David בְּרִבְבֹתָיו, his ten thousands.” Saul hears the difference (1Sa 18:8).
“A thousand shall fall at your side, and רְבָבָה at your right hand.”

senses.definition: In the plural, or as a round number, a host too great to count: Israel’s tribes, Yahweh’s holy ones, an enemy round about.

evidence.note: When the ark rested Moses said, “Return, Yahweh, to רִבְבוֹת אַלְפֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel”: the whole camp, counted by its thousands.
“They are רִבְבוֹת Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.”
Rebekah’s blessing: “Our sister, be you thousands of רְבָבָה.”
Yahweh came from Sinai “and came from רִבְבֹת קֹדֶשׁ, the ten thousands of holiness”: the holy ones with him.
“I will not be afraid of רִבְבוֹת עָם, ten thousands of people, who have set themselves against me round about.”
“Will Yahweh be pleased with thousands of rams, with רִבְבוֹת of rivers of oil?”
“My beloved is white and ruddy, chief מֵרְבָבָה, among ten thousand.”
“רְבָבָה, as the growth of the field, I made you”: made you increase beyond counting.
“The Lord came with myriads (μυριάσιν) of his holy ones”, the words of Deu 33:2.

evidence.locator: Deu.33.2, מֵרִבְבֹת → μυριάσιν; 1Sa.18.7 → μυριάσιν; Gen.24.60 → μυριάδων; μυριάς renders רְבָבָה ×12

evidence.note: “Behold, the Lord came ἐν ἁγίαις μυριάσιν αὐτοῦ”, Deu 33:2.
“To Mount Zion … and to μυριάσιν of angels.”
“Their number was μυριάδες μυριάδων and thousands of thousands”, Dan 7:10.
“How many μυριάδες of Jews there are who believe.”

parallels.note: Thousand, the number below it, set in the line before it.

words.summary: The later form of רְבָבָה (also רִבּוֹא), used in exact sums, mostly in the books after the exile: “four רִבּוֹא two thousand three hundred and sixty” (Ezr 2:64).

senses.definition: Ten thousand as a unit of an exact count, of people or of money; dual “twenty thousand”.

evidence.note: “The whole assembly together was אַרְבַּע רִבּוֹא, four ten-thousands, two thousand three hundred and sixty”: 42,360. Also Neh 7:66.
Nineveh, with “more than twelve רִבּוֹ of men”, 120,000, who do not know their right hand from their left.
Gold, “darics רִבּוֹ”, ten thousand; bronze “רִבּוֹ and eight thousand talents”, 18,000.
“Gold, darics שְׁתֵּי רִבּוֹא”, twenty thousand.
“The chariots of God are רִבֹּתַיִם, twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them, Sinai, in the holy place.”
The king of the south “shall cast down רִבֹּאוֹת, tens of thousands, but he shall not prevail”.

words.summary: Showers of rain, always plural, set beside מָטָר “rain”, טַל “dew” and מַלְקוֹשׁ “latter rain”. Its tie to the root is likely the many drops or abundance of the rain; Arabic rabāb “clouds” and rabab “much water” point the same way, but the link is not sure.

senses.definition: Heavy or abundant rain on the land, which God gives or withholds.

evidence.note: “My teaching shall drop as the rain (מָטָר), my speech distil as the dew, as small rain on the tender grass, and כִרְבִיבִים on the herb.”
“Therefore רְבִבִים have been withheld, and there has been no latter rain (מַלְקוֹשׁ).”
“Are there any among the vanities of the nations that cause rain? Or can the heavens give רְבִבִים? Are you not he, Yahweh our God?”
The king “shall come down like rain (מָטָר) on the mown grass, כִּרְבִיבִים that water the earth”.
“You make it soft בִּרְבִיבִים; you bless its springing.”
The remnant of Jacob among many peoples “as dew from Yahweh, כִּרְבִיבִים upon the grass, that waits not for man”.

evidence.locator: Deu.32.2, רְבִיבִים → νιφετός; the only aligned rendering, and a word the New Testament does not use

words.summary: A second verb of the same spelling, “shoot”, certain only at Gen 49:23, where archers shoot at Joseph. Its tie to רבב “be many” is not clear, and no cognate yet shows it; רָבָה “shoot” (Gen 21:20, רֹבֶה קַשָּׁת “an archer”) is the same sense under another root.

senses.definition: To shoot arrows at someone.

evidence.note: Joseph: “The בַּעֲלֵי חִצִּים, masters of arrows, embittered him, וָרֹבּוּ, and shot, and hated him.”
“He sent out his arrows and scattered them, and lightnings רָב, and confused them”: either “he shot” lightnings, in parallel with the arrows, or “many” lightnings.

words.summary: An archer, a noun of the verb “shoot”; clear in Jer 50:29 and Job 16:13 only. Most of the uses counted under its key are רַבִּים “many”, filed here by spelling. Like the verb, its tie to “be many” is not clear.

senses.definition: One who shoots arrows, in war or as a figure of God’s attack.

evidence.note: “Call together רַבִּים against Babylon, all who bend the bow”: archers, defined by the parallel.
“His רַבָּיו surround me; he splits my kidneys and does not spare”: God’s archers.
“רַב מְחוֹלֵל־כֹּל, and he who hires a fool and he who hires passers-by”: perhaps “an archer who wounds all”, perhaps “a master who forms all”; the sense here is not certain.

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic’s word for “great”, with the plural רַבְרְבִין (רַבְרְבָן): a great image, great God, great beasts, “Babylon the great”, a mouth speaking great things. As a noun, as in Hebrew, the chief of a body of men.

senses.definition: Great in size, power or importance; in the plural רַבְרְבָן, great things, boasts.

evidence.note: “Behold, a great image (צְלֵם … רַב)”, its brightness excellent.
The stone that struck the image became טוּר רַב, a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
“אֱלָהּ רַב, the great God, has made known to the king what shall be hereafter.”
“The house of אֱלָהָא רַבָּא, the great God.”
“Is not this בָּבֶל רַבְּתָא, Babylon the great, that I have built?” Revelation names the city the same (Rev 14:8; 18:2).
Four חֵיוָן רַבְרְבָן, great beasts, came up from the sea; “these great beasts are four kings” (Dan 7:17).
The little horn had “a mouth speaking רַבְרְבָן, great things”; also Dan 7:11, 20.
The beast was given “a mouth speaking μεγάλα”, the words of Dan 7:8.
“Babylon ἡ μεγάλη is fallen”, Dan 4:27’s name.
Belshazzar made לְחֶם רַב, a great feast, for a thousand of his lords.

senses.definition: As a noun in construct, the head of a body of officials: of the executioners, the prefects, the magicians.

evidence.note: Arioch, רַב־טַבָּחַיָּא, the chief of the king’s executioners.
The king made Daniel ruler of the province and רַב־סִגְנִין, chief of the prefects, over all the wise men of Babylon.
“Belteshazzar, רַב חַרְטֻמַיָּא, chief of the magicians.” Also Dan 5:11.
Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, Dan 4:27’s בָּבֶל רַבְּתָא.
στόμα λαλοῦν μεγάλα, Dan 7:8’s פֻם מְמַלִּל רַבְרְבָן.

words.summary: Always plural with a suffix, “his lords”: the great men of a king’s court, from the reduplicated plural of רַב.

senses.definition: The great men of the king’s court, who feast with him, counsel him and seal with him.

evidence.note: Belshazzar made a great feast “לְרַבְרְבָנוֹהִי אֲלַף, for a thousand of his lords”.
The king, “his lords, his wives and his concubines” drank from the temple vessels.
Nebuchadnezzar: “my counsellors וְרַבְרְבָנַי, and my lords, sought me.”
The king sealed the den “with his own signet and with the signet of רַבְרְבָנוֹהִי, his lords”.

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic’s ten thousand, once only, of the host before the Ancient of Days: “ten thousand times ten thousand” (Dan 7:10).

senses.definition: Ten thousand, doubled in “myriad of myriads” for a host beyond counting.

evidence.note: “A thousand thousands served him, וְרִבּוֹ רִבְבָן, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him; the judgment was set and the books were opened.”
Round the throne, “μυριάδες μυριάδων and thousands of thousands”: Dan 7:10.

cognates.gloss: lord, master, chief, owner; (verb rabba) be lord over, rule; rear, bring up
cognates.note: The Arabic word for the head of a thing or people, as Hebrew רַב is the chief of a body of men; Arabic keeps it of God too, which Hebrew does not.

evidence.note: “A lord, a possessor, an owner, or a proprietor … and a lord, master, or chief; or a lord, master, or chief, to whom obedience is paid.”
“He was, or became, its رَبّ, or lord … had possession of it, and command, or authority, over it”; also “He reared, fostered, brought up”.

cognates.gloss: rubbah: a large company; a myriad, ten thousand; rubba: many a
cognates.note: Lane’s sources give رُبَّةٌ and رِبَّةٌ as “a myriad, i.e. ten thousand”, as רְבָבָה; and the particle رُبَّ is used “to denote a large number”, “many a”, as רַב many.

evidence.note: “A party … or a large assembly or company: or a myriad; i. e. ten thousand.”
“Or it is used to denote a large number … it may be rendered Many … with مَا affixed, Many times, many a time, oftentimes.”

cognates.gloss: rabāb: clouds; rabab: much water collected together
cognates.note: Clouds and abundant water from the same Arabic root may stand beside רְבִיבִים “showers”, though the root’s sense of multitude may lie behind both independently.

evidence.note: “Clouds: or white clouds … or clouds consisting of an accumulation of parts.”
“Much water, collected together.”

cognates.note: Both senses of the Hebrew in one Ugaritic word: “great” of a city (udm rbt, Great Udum), and the chief of a group in construct, rb khnm “chief of the priests”, as רַב־טַבָּחִים.

evidence.note: “rb /rabb-/ … ‘great’; rb … ‘chief’ (cf. H., Aram. rab(b-), ‘great,’ ‘chief’; Phoen. rb, Arab. rabb ‘chief’)”; rbt /rabbat-/ “lady”.
“/rabbu/ (‘great’ >) ‘head, chairman’ … a genitive after rb indicates the group or institution over which the rb is head (cf. rb khnm …)”.

cognates.note: The numeral of the same root, with a dual as Hebrew רִבֹּתַיִם (Psa 68:18).

evidence.note: “The numeral ‘10,000’ is written rbt. The root is /r-b-b/ … (cf. H. and Aram. ribbo, H. rababa). This numeral occurs also in the dual: rbtm (cf. H. ribbótáyim).”
“rbt 1.24:20 ‘10,000’ (H., Aram. ribbo; H. rəbaba)”.

cognates.gloss: great number, many; ten thousand; chief, head, governor, general; great, senior
cognates.note: Phoenician and Punic use rb for every sense the Hebrew has: rb “great number”, its antonym msk “few” (as רֹב against מְעֹט); rb “ten thousand”; rb in construct for the head of priests, of a hundred, of the army, as רַב־טַבָּחִים; and rb “great”, rendered magnus in Roman sources.

evidence.note: “RB I [Heb. rob] n.m. GREAT NUMBER, MANY, KAI 26 A III 4/6 (Ph) … ‘many days many years!’ Obs. The antonym is msk, ‘few’”; “RB II [Heb. ribbō] n.m. TEN THOUSAND”.

evidence.locator: pp. 438–439, RB IV; RB V; RB VI
evidence.note: “RB V … CHIEF, HEAD of a group or occupation … rb khnm, ‘Chief of Priests’ … rb m’t, ‘Head of One Hundred’ … 2. GOVERNOR”; “RB VI [Heb. rab] adj. 1. GREAT … 2. SENIOR … 3. pl. MANY”.

cognates.gloss: great, big; elder; chief, commander; (verb) be or become great
cognates.note: Akkadian rabû, in the construct rab, is “great” and “chief”, as Hebrew רַב, and also “elder, eldest”, as רַב against צָעִיר (Gen 25:23). Its verb is III-weak, nearer Hebrew רָבָה than רָבַב.

evidence.note: “big; chief; elder; eldest; great; large; magnate; overseer; powerful; senior; superior”.
“be(come) big; be(come) great; be promoted; bring up a child”.

cognates.note: The Assyrian title borrowed whole as רַב־שָׁקֵה, the Rabshakeh of 2Ki 18 and Isa 36: rab “chief” of the šāqû, cupbearers.

evidence.locator: tsae x000078740, rab šāqê [chief cupbearer] N; also armep x000146170, rab-šāqê

cognates.gloss: chief eunuch (an Assyrian and Babylonian officer)
cognates.note: Borrowed as רַב־סָרִיס, with Hebrew סָרִיס for ša-rēši.

evidence.locator: tsae x000078790, rab ša-rēši [chief eunuch] N

cognates.gloss: large, great, numerous; senior; chief, teacher
cognates.note: The Targums’ Aramaic keeps the word as scripture’s does: great, numerous, and chief; רַבָּן, רַבָּנָא “chief, teacher”.

evidence.note: “large, great, numerous; senior. Targ. Josh. XXII, 10. Targ. Y. Deut. I, 28. Targ. Gen. I, 16.”
“chief; teacher. Targ. I Chr. XI, 11 … (h. text שר)”.
Targ. I Kings VIII, 63; Targ. Deut. XXXII, 30, where Hebrew has רְבָבָה.
“[large amount,] myriad, ten thousand. Peah III, 8 … one ten thousandth portion of my property.”

cognates.gloss: great; chief, master; ܪܒܝ rabbi, master; verb ܪܒ be made great

evidence.locator: lexemes 2906 RB (be made great, magnified), 2907 RBA (great; chief; master), 2916 RB; (rabbi; master), 2913 RBOL; (master), root 1722 RB

doctrine.statement: When Yahweh passed before Moses and proclaimed his name, he called himself “merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and רַב־חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת, abounding in steadfast love and truth” (Exo 34:6). The words are pleaded back to him by Moses for a rebellious people (Num 14:18), by the Levites after the exile (Neh 9:17), by David (Psa 86:15; 103:8), and by Joel and Jonah as the reason he turns from evil (Jol 2:13; Jon 4:2); David asks for mercy “according to the multitude (רֹב) of your compassions” (Psa 51:3). From the verses: what the name declares is a God whose steadfast love is more than his people’s sin, and his people appeal to that abundance, not to their own deserving.

Isaiah’s servant “shall make many (לָרַבִּים) righteous, and he shall bear their iniquities”, and “he bore the sin of many (רַבִּים)” (Isa 53:11–12). Jesus says he came “to give his life a ransom for many” (Mrk 10:45); Hebrews, that “Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many” (Heb 9:28); and Paul, that “by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous” (Rom 5:19). From the verses: the “many” are those the one servant’s death and obedience make righteous; the word sets the one against the many he bears for.

Daniel is told that “many (רַבִּים) of those who sleep in the dust of the ground shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to reproach and everlasting contempt” (Dan 12:2). The dead are said to sleep in the dust, and their awaking is out of the dust, to a judgment with two outcomes. The verse says “many”, not “all” of the sleepers: it describes a raising of some of the dead, not of everyone who has died.

Yahweh came from Sinai “from the ten thousands (רִבְבֹת) of holiness” (Deu 33:2); “the chariots of God are twice ten thousand (רִבֹּתַיִם), thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them, Sinai, in the holy place” (Psa 68:18); before the Ancient of Days “a thousand thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand (רִבּוֹ רִבְבָן) stood before him” when the judgment was set (Dan 7:10). The New Testament takes up the same count: the Lord coming “with myriads of his holy ones” to execute judgment (Jud 1:14), “myriads of angels” at Mount Zion (Heb 12:22), and myriads of myriads round the throne (Rev 5:11). From the verses: the host who attend God at the giving of the law and at the judgment are beyond counting, and they come with the Lord when he judges.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Numbers 10 (רִבְבוֹת, Num 10:36); no word of the root occurs in Leviticus 23. BDB keys and token counts: the keys are matched to tokens by spelling, so t.ae.ab (adjective), t.ae.ac (chief) and t.af.ab (archer) share almost all their tokens (רַב, רַבִּים, רַבָּה), and t.af.aa (shoot) counts every רָב; the use counts of the chief, archer and shoot words are therefore far too high (archer is clear only at Jer 50:29 and Job 16:13; shoot at Gen 49:23). t.ae.aa likewise counts the לָרֹב of רֹב and some רַבּוּ the morphology gives to רבה. xt.ab.ab counts Hebrew רַב tokens by spelling as well as Daniel’s and Ezra’s Aramaic. Zero-token cross-references claimed: t.ak.ac and t.ao.ad (רַב־מָג, רַב־שָׁקֶה) on the chief noun, t.bh.ad (רוֹב) on רֹב, xt.ad.ad (רַבְרְבִין) on Aramaic רַב, xt.ad.ae on רַבְרְבָן. Left unclaimed: t.ad.am, t.ad.an and t.aj.ab, “see” references filed under other headwords. Left out: the names יָרָבְעָם Jeroboam (t.ae.aj), a person, for names/; and the places רַבָּה Rabbah (t.ae.ad), רַבִּית Rabbith (t.ae.ah) and בַּת־רַבִּים Bath-rabbim (b.ca.au). The verb רָבָה “be many” and its nouns (מַרְבִּית, תַּרְבּוּת…) and רָבָה II “shoot” are the root רבה, a separate entry; Aramaic רְבָה “grow great” (Dan 2:48 רַבִּי, Dan 4:19) and רְבוּ “greatness” likewise belong there. Akkadian rabû is III-weak and may answer to רבה rather than רבב; it is entered here because its rab “chief” is the title Hebrew borrows. Rab-mag: no Akkadian rab mugi found in Oracc; its second element is left unexplained. Peshitta words not entered as syc words: SEDRA root 1722 gives ܪܒܘܬܐ “myriad” (Luk 12:1; Act 21:20; Heb 12:22; Jud 1:14; Rev 5:11 are the Greek μυριάς verses; the Peshitta’s wording there not checked) and ܪܒܝ “rabbi”. Segert’s glossary entries for rb and rbt cited by section, printed page not found in the OCR. Krahmalkov pp. 437–439 read from the local text layer only. Not consulted: DULAT; Ge’ez (Dillmann, Leslau). Open questions: (1) whether “shoot” and “archer” belong to this root or to רבה II; (2) Psa 18:15 רָב “shot” or “many”; (3) Pro 26:10; (4) Ezk 16:7 רְבָבָה read as “myriad, I made you”; (5) whether Dan 12:2’s “many” should be pressed as doctrine as written.
